classification.difficultyReason: No diagram, and the student is not told which side is the hypotenuse. They must see that there are two cases: 20 cm as the hypotenuse, giving 16, and both given sides as legs, giving sqrt(544)≈23.32. Each case is a single Pythagoras step plus rounding. This is harder than the signposted two-step surd chain in p33-q1 because the case split is unsignposted. It is easier than p34-q3 and p14-q7, where more steps or a justification are needed.

content.prompt: A right-angled triangle has two sides of length 12 cm and 20 cm. Find the two possible lengths of the third side. Give any non-whole-number answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
If the third side is a shorter side, 20 cm is the hypotenuse:
$$\begin{align*}a&=\sqrt{20^2-12^2}\\a&=\sqrt{256}\\a&=16\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
If the third side is the hypotenuse:
$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{12^2+20^2}\\h&=\sqrt{544}\\h&\approx23.32\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
